According to British gaming outlet Eurogamer on the 24th, Cyberleek, the anonymous hacker who breached Rockstar Games in August and leaked the game's entire development files, recently released the executable file for the Xbox version of GTA 6.
After leaking the full game build, Cyberleek had been receiving cryptocurrency donations while releasing stolen files and gameplay footage. Cyberleek had not released the executable (exe) file needed to run the game until making it public five days after the game's release.
A group of developers called "Project Leonida" downloaded the files released by Cyberleek and reportedly modified and ported the Xbox version to run on PCs with the help of the artificial intelligence (AI) tool Claude.
According to Eurogamer, one hacker reportedly managed to boot the game on a PC as far as the initial setup screen but failed to enter the game itself. They claim it will take about a week for the build to become playable on a PC.
GTA 6 was released worldwide on the 19th for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games typically releases games on consoles first and follows with a PC version about a year later.
But amid growing concern about the August hack and the prospect of an unofficial port using AI, some expect the company to bring forward the PC version's release to the first quarter of next year.

articles.t: Rockstar Games kills unauthorized 'GTA 6' PC port, for obvious reasons
articles.chapeau: Just wait for the official PC version of the game to come out.
articles.txt:
Don't try to port Grand Theft Auto VI to PC yourself — or you'll potentially find yourself in big legal trouble.
GTA 6 may finally be out on Xbox and PlayStation 5, but that doesn't help out the PC gaming faithful, who still have much longer to wait for their version of the game.
As a result, some impatient gamers have recently attempted to create PC ports of the game themselves. Notorious GTA 6 leaker, Cyberleek, also recently released an executable .exe file of the Xbox build of the game, which helped those efforts. Even without Cyberleek, these efforts were probably inevitable, as new AI tools have led to a surge in PS5 jailbreaks and unauthorized ports of classic video games.
However, Rockstar Games' parent company, Take-Two Interactive, clearly does not approve of these unofficial attempts to bring GTA 6 to PC ahead of schedule. On Monday, the company had the biggest GTA 6 PC port project, known as Leonida, taken down. So far, GTA 6 has generated billions of dollars, and the PC version could bring in billions more. And when it comes to protecting their IP, Take-Two and Rockstar aren't messing around.
GitHub, where the project was hosted, posted a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) notice it received from Take-Two.
"We are the IP Enforcement Team for Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., parent company of Rockstar Games," the notice reads. "We are writing to submit a takedown request regarding ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the 2900+ forks attached to it that infringes upon Take-Two's copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI."
Take-Two explains how the project is based on the company's stolen IP, the Xbox version of GTA 6 . The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile
"On November 20, 2026, stolen game files from an Xbox Series build of Grand Theft Auto VI were publicly distributed," the takedown notice reads. "The following day, this Leonida repository opened with the purpose of running the Xbox Series version of GTA VI on PC. Its README requires Xbox Series game files as input."
According to Take-Two, Leonida attempts to get around the IP issues by instructing project contributors to "bring your own files."
"This is intentionally misleading," Take-Two explains, pointing out that the files in question are the unauthorized GTA 6 files leaked by Cyberleek.
As our colleagues at PCMag point out , this is just one of many unauthorized projects attempting to bring GTA 6 to PC before the official version comes out. (Disclosure: Mashable and PCMag are both owned by the same parent company, Ziff Davis.) Other projects have reportedly managed to get the game's opening scene running on PC. Another has an extremely degraded version of the game running on Mac.
According to the Leonida project admin , Take-Two also successfully had the Discord server for the GTA 6 porting project taken down as well, so it does seem like the company is going to ramp up its takedowns of any attempted GTA 6 ports.
GTA 6 for PC has no official release date. However, GameBeat recently reported that the PC version may be released in early 2027, well before most gamers expected.

S'informer ▪ Altcoins Résumer cet article avec : ChatGPT Perplexity Grok Cyberleek voulait propulser son memecoin à 15 millions de dollars de capitalisation grâce aux fuites de GTA 6. L’opération se solde par un échec. Le 23 novembre 2026, l’auteur présumé des divulgations a finalement publié le fichier exécutable d’une version Xbox du jeu. Le lendemain, sa crypto affichait une valorisation de seulement 1,36 million de dollars. Même le lancement de l’un des jeux vidéo les plus attendus de la décennie n’aura pas suffi.
Lisez-nous sur Google News En bref Cyberleek aurait publié le fichier exécutable de GTA 6 le 23 novembre. Son memecoin reste environ 91 % en dessous de son objectif de capitalisation. Les volumes horaires observés lors de la dernière fuite sont près de 29 fois inférieurs au pic enregistré en août. GTA 6 au cœur d’un pari crypto raté Le 19 novembre, jour du lancement officiel de GTA 6 sur consoles, Cyberleek affirme détenir une version presque complète du jeu sur Xbox. Environ 209 Go de fichiers auraient été diffusés, à l’exception du principal fichier exécutable.
Sa publication anticipée devait dépendre des performances de la crypto CYBERLEEK. Le token avait pourtant déjà connu son heure de gloire. En août, la crypto de Cyberleek avait atteint 25 millions de dollars avant de s’effondrer de 46 % en une journée , après plusieurs ventes attribuées à son créateur.
Cyberleek espérait reproduire cette envolée. En octobre, il avait fixé un premier objectif de capitalisation à 30 millions de dollars. En novembre, ses ambitions sont descendues à 15 millions.
Le marché crypto n’a pas suivi. Au 24 novembre, CYBERLEEK s’échangeait autour de 0,00136 dollar, pour une capitalisation proche de 1,36 million et un volume quotidien de 752 000 dollars.
Cyberleek a néanmoins tenu sa promesse de diffuser le fichier le 23 novembre, indépendamment du résultat financier. L’auteur affirme que les fonds collectés doivent financer un projet secret, sans rapport direct avec GTA 6. Aucun élément public ne permet actuellement de vérifier cette affirmation.
Les données on-chain de Bitquery permettent de mesurer la perte d’intérêt des investisseurs. Entre le 16 et le 18 novembre, CYBERLEEK a perdu 45 % de sa valeur. Le jour du lancement de GTA 6, le token a rebondi de 41 %, avant de progresser encore de 16 % le lendemain.
Les deux journées suivantes ont effacé une partie de ces gains. Le 23 novembre, la publication du fichier exécutable a provoqué une nouvelle réaction du marché. L’heure la plus active a enregistré environ 186 600 dollars de transactions.
En août, lors des premières fuites, le record horaire atteignait 5,47 millions de dollars. Près de 29 fois plus. Cyberleek disposait pourtant cette fois d’un argument promotionnel beaucoup plus important que quelques vidéos inédites : les fichiers d’une version présumée du jeu.
Certains investisseurs ont surtout profité du rebond pour vendre. Bitquery a identifié cinq portefeuilles ayant réalisé environ 123 000 dollars de ventes, sans aucun achat entre le 19 et le 23 novembre.
Ces montants ne correspondent pas nécessairement à leurs bénéfices. L’épisode rappelle les difficultés rencontrées sur ce marché, où près de 94 % des traders de memecoins Solana suivis dans une précédente étude affichaient des pertes. Pour CYBERLEEK, la publication des fichiers n’aura finalement provoqué qu’un regain temporaire d’activité.
Cyberleek avait probablement commis une erreur dès l’annonce de son calendrier. En promettant de publier le fichier le 23 novembre, même si son objectif financier n’était pas atteint, il supprimait une grande partie de l’intérêt d’acheter sa crypto. Les joueurs pouvaient simplement patienter quelques jours.
Pourquoi acheter un token risqué pour obtenir plus rapidement quelque chose qui devait devenir accessible gratuitement ? L’affaire a également donné naissance à plusieurs cryptomonnaies imitatrices. Un token baptisé Justice For Cyberleek est notamment apparu sur Pump.fun le 23 novembre.
Les risques concernent aussi les joueurs. Dès le 3 novembre, les chercheurs de Netcraft avaient recensé 121 nouveaux noms de domaine reprenant l’identité de Cyberleek. Certains proposaient de prétendues versions de GTA 6 contenant des fichiers suspects.

articles.t: GTA 6 PC port projects are already going offline
articles.chapeau: Project Leonida lost its GitHub page and its Discord was reportedly taken down after the GTA 6 Xbox leak. No GTA 6 PC port is playable yet, either.
articles.txt:
The GTA 6 Xbox leak hasn’t yielded a playable PC port, and Rockstar hasn’t confirmed whether it requested the removal of Project Leonida’s Discord server.
0:00 Unofficial GTA 6 PC port projects are going offline days after a leaked Xbox build was released.
None of the projects has made GTA 6 playable on PC. Project Leonida, which aimed to get the Xbox Series X build running on PC, lost its GitHub page. VGC reports a claim that Leonida’s Discord server was taken down at the request of Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two.
The server had around 179,000 members, with 74,000 online. There’s no evidence of emails from Rockstar or Discord, and Rockstar and Take-Two have said nothing.
On 18 November, Take-Two used DMCA takedowns against unofficial GTA 5 ports on GitHub. In August, it subpoenaed Discord for data on Cyberleek, the account behind the GTA 6 leak. Rockstar’s modding guidelines also restrict unofficial ports.
Leonida’s GitHub page returned a 404 error, not a DMCA notice. The error points more towards the project’s operators having deleted the page, but it doesn’t prove they did.
Cyberleek released the Xbox build on 19 November without the executable, promising to release it sooner if a meme coin reached a $15 million target. The coin missed that target, but Cyberleek released the executable the following Monday anyway. According to Decrypt, the GTA6Modding Discord server was removed the next day, and other groups, including Chasm, locked down their servers.
Many projects are using AI chatbots such as Claude to write their code. Two projects, VIctory and XCL, can load the game world, but neither can run it in a playable state. Don’t download anything advertised as GTA 6 for PC; some carry infostealers.

articles.txt:
The much-anticipated GTA 6 was recently released on Xbox Series S|X and PlayStation 5 (Pro) consoles—on November 19, to be exact. However, the PC version is still missing, which drew the ire of the Cyberleek group, which leaked an Xbox build of the game a few days ago. Yesterday, as promised, the group released the game’s executable file—the missing piece of the puzzle.
The fact that Rockstar is (once again) skipping the PC version at the game’s launch seems to have seriously upset the hackers at Cyberleek , who were behind numerous gameplay leaks prior to the game’s release. On the game’s release day, they published a nearly complete build of the Xbox version of the game with almost all the files—only the executable was missing—and it wasn’t until yesterday that the group decided to share the prized file, followed by the message: “The exe is out. Always free .” Along with this, the SHA-256 hashes of the executable were also published.
However, this does not mean the game will run natively on PC ; no, there is still a lot of work to be done, since the game continues to rely on console-specific services. The same goes for memory management and graphical interfaces. Developers must therefore adapt the game’s code to make it PC-compatible . Nevertheless, the development of an unofficial port is entering a new phase, and things are likely to move very quickly. Admittedly, projects like Project Leonida had already begun even before the executable was shared, but that project seems to have stalled, as its GitHub repository has been closed.
Meanwhile, Rockstar appears to be keeping quiet, as the studio has not issued any press releases or responded to these two major leaks. In contrast, we can only assume that the studio finds itself in a delicate situation, as they still need to work on the PC version, but they’re now competing with independent developers who can distribute the PC port for free before they do—which poses a significant financial risk as well as a major blow to the studio’s reputation. In short, we’re following all of this closely—the rest of the story promises to be fascinating!

articles.t: GTA VI sur PC : le portage non officiel CGBJ lance déjà le jeu
articles.chapeau: Après la fuite de l'exécutable, cinq portages non officiels de GTA VI avancent sur PC. CGBJ atteint déjà le jeu, sans éclairage, et reste privé.
articles.txt:
Il n'aura pas fallu plus de vingt-quatre heures. Depuis que CyberLeek a publié lundi 23 novembre l'exécutable de la build Xbox Series de GTA VI , plusieurs portages PC non officiels ont réussi à faire démarrer le jeu. Et selon DSOGaming , l'un d'eux, baptisé CGBJ , atteint déjà les phases de jeu, alors que Leonida , le projet le plus attendu, a jeté l'éponge dans la nuit.
Le site recense cinq émulateurs ou portages majeurs : CGBJ , VIctory , XCL , Xbox2Windows et TuxBox . Les deux derniers parviennent à lancer GTA VI et à afficher sa première image. XCL et VIctory vont plus loin, jusqu'au menu principal, et faisaient figure de favoris avant l'apparition de CGBJ.
Les deux projets ne s'y prennent pas tout à fait comme Leonida, qui misait sur la recompilation statique du code du jeu . XCL , écrit en Rust et publié sous licence GPL-2.0 le 20 novembre, se présente comme une couche de compatibilité entre la Xbox Series et Windows, dans l'esprit de Wine ou de Proton . Il n'émule pas le processeur : le code x64 du jeu tourne directement sur le PC, tandis que XCL réécrit de son côté les bibliothèques système de la console, comme kernelx.dll ou d3d12_xs.dll, et recompile les shaders RDNA2 de la console en shaders PC. Son dépôt affirme faire déjà tourner entièrement Minecraft Preview , Unicorn Overlord , Fortnite et XDefiant , dans la limite de leurs services en ligne.
VIctory , lui aussi écrit en Rust, sous licence GPL-3.0, est né dans la soirée du 23 novembre avec un seul objectif : faire tourner GTA VI sur Windows à partir des fichiers fournis par l'utilisateur. Son état des lieux est précis : le jeu démarre, affiche ses écrans de premier lancement, sa vidéo d'introduction avec le son et ses menus à 30 images par seconde, puis charge le monde en une cinquantaine de secondes. Mais une fois dans la première mission, seul le titre s'affiche, la scène reste sombre et chaque image prend de 0,5 à 1,8 seconde. Une partie des shaders n'est pas encore traduite, et le projet prévient que l'entrée dans le monde peut figer la carte graphique au point de forcer Windows à relancer son pilote. Les deux dépôts cumulent déjà plusieurs milliers d'étoiles sur GitHub.
CGBJ est une version privée de VIctory qui reprend une partie des travaux de XCL. D'après DSOGaming, sa dernière version permet de se déplacer à la manette, de parler aux personnages non joueurs et d'ouvrir le menu du jeu. Un résultat obtenu en moins de vingt-quatre heures, qui reste très loin d'une version jouable : il n'y a pas d'éclairage et les performances sont mauvaises. John Papadopoulos , qui s'attendait à voir Leonida arriver le premier à ce stade, juge toutefois ces images légitimes, contrairement aux fausses vidéos qui montraient le jeu tourner avec de superbes graphismes.
Il appelle malgré tout à la prudence : les images semblent authentiques et PortWatch les aurait confirmées, mais elles pourraient encore être fausses. Derrière CGBJ, XCL et VIctory plantent pour l'instant au moment d'entrer dans le jeu, mais ce n'est peut-être qu'une question d'heures avant qu'ils ne franchissent eux aussi cette étape. La prochaine sera d'afficher des images correctes, sans artefacts, avant de s'attaquer aux performances.
Les progrès s'enchaînent en effet. Sur X, le compte itsawful911 a publié mardi matin une nouvelle vidéo en assurant que les shaders commencent à fonctionner et que les cheveux des personnages s'affichent nettement mieux. Il se risquait même à prédire des visuels « presque parfaits » d'ici la fin de la journée, avant de passer à l'optimisation.
Pour les joueurs, ces avancées ne changent presque rien. CGBJ est un projet privé, impossible à télécharger, et ni XCL ni VIctory ne proposent de version publique. Leur code source est bien accessible sur GitHub et peut être compilé, mais il ne fournit aucun fichier du jeu : il suppose de disposer de la build qui a fuité, ce qui n'a rien de légal. Toute archive présentée comme un GTA VI prêt à installer est donc à fuir, d'autant que de faux portages truffés de logiciels malveillants circulent depuis des mois.
Ces projets avancent par ailleurs sous la menace de Take-Two , qui avait déjà multiplié les demandes de retrait depuis la diffusion de la build par CyberLeek . Rockstar n'a toujours annoncé aucune version PC officielle, qu'un rapport paru en octobre situait au premier trimestre 2027. D'ici là, la course entre les portages non officiels promet de se jouer à l'heure près.

Leaker Cyberleek Releases The Xbox Build Executable for GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Not even a month into the GTA 6 glory, the leaker publishes the complete .exe file as an "early Christmas present."
articles.txt:
Not even a month into the GTA 6 glory, the leaker publishes the complete .exe file as an "early Christmas present."
Less than a week after GTA 6, which had been in production for over a decade, finally had its moment as " the biggest entertainment launch in history across all industries ," an infamous leaker made its full build public. Cyberleek posted the Xbox build executable online, just as promised .
Originally, Cyberleek only posted a near-complete GTA 6 build without the .exe. The missing precious executable was the very piece of the puzzle tying everything together and making it possible to run the build. The leaker stated that the full file would be out once their crypto coin hit the $15 million market cap. Otherwise, they would just give it out on November 23 – whichever happens first. The bold $15-million financial goal was out of reach, so the leaker released the file on November 23 as an "early Christmas present."
In the "release note," Cyberleek also commented on Take-Two Interactive's ongoing efforts to track them down.
"Months of takedowns, subpoenas, and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on, and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has," the cocky statement from the leaker reads.
This leak paves the way for developers to create a fully playable PC build way before Rockstar even announces one. However, since creating a full-scale version of the game in a short period of time is unrealistic, the first PC version of GTA 6 will very likely be an AI-made emulation of the game.
Although many players are excited to see the free .exe file just a few days into the launch, other users are not as blindly optimistic about the leak. Considering how quickly and unapologetically the industry shifted from physical copies to digital downloads as a more profitable distribution model, the Cyberleek situation might be the perfect excuse for publishers to give up on the concept of players owning a game entirely.
With this in mind, whether what Cyberleek is doing is ethical or not is a big question. "CYBERLEEK is about fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry. It was never about damaging the players," the leaker's note says. However, no matter their intentions, these leaks might eventually harm the players. The "billion-dollar companies" Cyberleek refers to are still doing fine after the leaks, but the way they approach game distribution might change, and players will be the ones affected by it.

articles.t: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects": GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek claims to have released crimsim's Xbox executable and denies crypto grifting
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has claimed to have released the executable file for an Xbox build of the game.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 leaker or leakers Cyberleek claim to to have released the main executable file for an alleged Xbox build of the game that they asserted they'd lobbed onto the net last week. In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.
Referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects". As of writing, the legitimacy of the executable doesn't appear to have been independently verified, meaning it could still just turn out to be a pile of malware or something similarly dodgy. Needless to say, given that and the fact software piracy is illegal, not touching it - or any of the other files Cyberleek claim to have posted - with a barge pole is the sensible thing to do.
Cyberleek have been bigging up the idea that these files they've been releasing could result in GTA 6 running on PC sharpish, via a modified version cobbled together with generative AI . That might happen, but I'm seriously skeptical that if it were to, it wouldn't just be dodgy jankware than runs like piss, rather than anything that'd compare remotely well to an official PC port.
Thus far, it appears a group of would-be recompilers going by Project Leonida may have got the game to start booting on PC, but they since look to have disappeared and scrubbed their established online presence.
All of this again raises the question of whether the threat of any sort of bodged PC recreation coming out of this alleged executable release may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between this month's console release and its eventual Windows release, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year.
Returning to Cyberleek's latest statement, the leaker or leakers have also taken the opportunity to insist that their attempts to pump up a crypto coin as part of the leaking is just for practical reasons rather than grifty ones , honest. "Every donation is a vote for more of this," they wrote. "Where the votes go, [Cyberleek] follows. Crypto here is just a tool - there is no other way to move funds without names."
Rockstar called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking". Along with parent company Take-Two, they began a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August, but that doesn't seem to to have deterred Cyberleek, if indeed the people leaking under the name are still the same ones as in the summer.
